articles.body: Shopify takes care of hosting, security updates and the checkout, so a store can go live quickly. What it does not do is decide how your store looks, how your products are organised or which apps and custom code you add. Those decisions are made by whoever builds the store, and they shape how fast it loads, how easy it is to run and what it costs you to change later. This guide explains what to look for when you choose a Shopify developer or agency. What does a Shopify developer actually do? "Shopify developer" covers several kinds of work, and it helps to know which ones your project needs before you start talking to people: Store setup: products, collections, navigation, shipping zones, taxes, payment providers, policies and notifications.

articles.title: How to Read DMARC Reports Before You Move to p=reject
articles.excerpt: Most domains that have DMARC at all are sitting on p=none. Someone added the record while setting up email, pointed rua= at a mailbox, and the reports have been arriving every day since: small zip and…
articles.body: Most domains that have DMARC at all are sitting on p=none . Someone added the record while setting up email, pointed rua= at a mailbox, and the reports have been arriving every day since: small zip and gzip attachments from Google, Outlook and other receivers, usually unopened. Those files answer the one question you need settled before tightening the policy: who is sending mail with your domain in the From line, and would that mail survive p=quarantine or p=reject ? Below is how to read them with nothing more than dig , unzip and a small XML tool, and how to move up the policy ladder without losing invoices or password resets on the way. If SPF and DKIM aren't set up yet, start with how to set up business email on your own domain and come back once those records exist.

articles.title: How I Built an Edge-First AI Cartoon SaaS with Next.js, Cloudflare Workers & D1
articles.excerpt: As an indie maker, launching an AI-powered SaaS often presents a brutal dilemma: The Traditional Cloud Route: Spin up beefy VPS or Kubernetes clusters, pay idle costs 24/7, and battle cold-start laten…
articles.body: As an indie maker, launching an AI-powered SaaS often presents a brutal dilemma: The Traditional Cloud Route: Spin up beefy VPS or Kubernetes clusters, pay idle costs 24/7, and battle cold-start latency when users generate images across the globe. The Modern Edge Route: Go 100% serverless on edge infrastructure (zero cold starts, global micro-second TTFB, fraction of the hosting cost), but deal with tight memory constraints and emerging edge runtimes. I chose the second path. Over the past few months, I built and launched AI Cartoon Generator — a specialized creative studio designed for cartoon, anime, and comic creators. Instead of relying on a monolithic server, the entire platform runs on Cloudflare Workers using Next.js App Router (via OpenNext) , Cloudflare D1 , and R2 .

articles.title: What Happens When You Give a Classifier Some Game Sense?
articles.excerpt: I've been experimenting with a retro defense game in Rust called Signal / Siege. The question behind it is simple: how much can traditional game AI help a classifier? Incoming contacts approach a base…
articles.body: I've been experimenting with a retro defense game in Rust called Signal / Siege. The question behind it is simple: how much can traditional game AI help a classifier? Incoming contacts approach a base. Some are hostile, others should pass safely. The defense can scan, intercept, or activate a shield, but energy is limited. Spending too much on one contact can leave it unprepared for the next. That creates two connected problems: estimating what a contact might be, and deciding what to do about it. The video above shows three approaches: Bayes + Utility: Bayesian classification paired with a system that scores possible actions. Jev + Rules: Jev classification paired with simple rules and Bayesian backup.

An Anticrepuscular Rainbow Fan Explanation: This is an unusual rainbow. For one thing, the rainbow is not complete, appearing only in a sunlit fan — but that by itself is not very unusual. articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.
